A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and duplicated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original probing and representation-engineering experiments on four LLMs, prompt-sensitivity analyses, and additional empirical results in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and adds reverse representation-engineering results for Mistral and Phi-3 in Appendix A.7.

M1.justification: The linear probes and additive representation-steering rule remain unchanged. Section 2.2 clarifies the representation positions; Appendix A.7 tests the existing steering operation with its direction reversed as an experimental control.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same IFEval-based coverage, including IFEval-simple and the expanded instruction set in Appendix A.3. The new dataset rationale and reverse-steering experiment introduce no additional dataset, task, or domain.

E2.justification: Original outputs and random-direction steering remain the comparators in Table 4. The new reverse-steering experiment also compares against original outputs and random directions, without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix A.7 adds a reverse-steering condition with conservatively selected adjustment strengths intended to keep response quality comparable to random steering. Existing splits, decoding, evaluation metrics, and forward-steering settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.7 tests whether reversing the identified direction reduces instruction adherence in Mistral and Phi-3 while preserving comparable response quality. Existing sensitivity, layer/token, expanded-instruction, and PCA analyses remain; the removed appendix steering plot duplicated Figure 3.

E5.justification: The five-seed task-probing and three-seed main steering summaries retain their uncertainty-reporting practices. Table 12 extends the existing plus/minus format; its accompanying 'not significant' statement specifies no new statistical test, and no changed run counts are documented.

E6.justification: Tables 1–11 retain their numerical results. New Table 12 reports reverse-steering success rates of 0.54 ± 0.01 for Mistral and 0.60 ± 0.02 for Phi, compared with random-direction rates of 0.56 ± 0.02 and 0.63 ± 0.04, respectively.

T1.justification: No theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. The new prompt/response notation clarifies existing representation positions; the additive steering rule and transition-ratio definitions are retained.

C1.justification: v5 explicitly defines 'knowing internally' as representation information correlated with instruction-following success. Its abstract and introduction foreground the unseen-instruction-type generalization boundary, replacing the introduction's broader 'fundamental aspect' characterization. The principal contributions otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 and new Appendix A.6 expand the justification for simple, verifiable instructions, including potential errors and biases from LLM-based compliance evaluators. Appendix A.7 qualifies reverse steering as preliminary and its difference from random steering as not significant. Existing Section 6.3 limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v5 replaces future code/data release promises with an availability statement and a concrete GitHub repository address. Section 2.2 also specifies the prompt and response prefixes corresponding to first-, middle-, and last-token representations, clarifying the existing implementation.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to instruction-following benchmarks, truthfulness probing, and representation engineering remain unchanged. The expanded dataset rationale adds no cited work or new relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to the abstract, dataset motivation, representation explanation, author information, and acknowledgments. The appendix removes redundant steering discussion, renumbers the PCA section, and adds two sections; the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v5 adds Table 12, removes the duplicate steering plot formerly numbered Figure 6, and relocates the five-instruction PCA plot as Figure 6 instead of Figure 7. It also compacts the author block and adjusts figure placement and sizing, while retaining the existing visual designs.

improvement.justification: v5 improves precision through an explicit meaning of 'knowing internally', clearer generalization boundaries, and better explanations of representation inputs and dataset choice. It also supplies concrete code/data access information and a useful reverse-steering control. That experiment remains preliminary and is described as not significantly different from random steering, so the gains are modest while the established empirical evidence is preserved.
